full_judgment: 15. PW 2 Nazrul Islam stated in his evidence that Syed Ali Akanda, Hazrat Ali Akanda and Asgar Ali Akanda were three full brothers. Asgar Ali died leaving a son and wife. Syed Ali and Hazrat Ali sold 4.73 acres of land along with other lands to Reazuddin Khalifa in 1932 and Reazuddin Khalifa used to possess this land through bargardar accused Moyzuddin. He further stated that Reazuddin, Habib and Mojibor used to barga cultivate the case land. He stated that the C&B acquired this land during the year 1971 for the purpose of manufacturing brick and compensation was paid to its owner Reazuddin and his bargardars as compensation for crops. He also stated that a khatian was subsequently prepared in the name of Reazuddin. Eventually, Reazuddin gifted in 1975 this land by a registered heba-bil-ewaz deed in favour of his two wives Aimona and Belayetunnessa. He also stated that in the year 1984 he purchased 2.63 acres of land in case plot No. 107 from the three sons of Aimona and Belayetunnessa while Abul Hossain Akanda purchased the remaining portion of 2 other sons. He aslo stated that he purchased 33 decimals of land from Abul Hossain while bargadar Habibur Rahman purchased some land from Aiman Nessa after they went into possession of the case land. He went on to state that Moyzuddin started creating troubles and threatened to forcibly take away paddy from the case land following which a salish was held and the village elders forbade him to forcibly take away paddy from the case land when accused Moyzuddin threatened to file a pre-emption case against him if he was not given the land in Bogra. He stated that 15 days thereafter Moyzuddin gave out that he had interest in the case land and produced a photo copy of a deed before the salish but subsequently he took it away. Thereafter on the advice of the salisadars he enquired about the matter in the local Sub-Registrar''''s Office. Subsequently, it transpired that accused Moyzuddin had filed a suit in the civil Court for correction of the records of rights. On enquiry, it was found that there was no index of the disputed deed of gift bearing No. 672, following which he filed the case in the Court of the local Magistrate. This petition of complaint has been marked as Ext. 16.
